## Control panel

- North star: produce one exhaustive, source-anchored current-state ledger that lets E/F choose laws and evidence-only work without inventing owners or gaps.
- Current claim: all 615 frozen donor items and eight campaign seeds have exactly one disposition against the pinned baselines; candidate coverage is 623/623.
- Latest product signal: 177 rows are SATISFIED, 343 PARTIAL, 58 ABSENT, 29 RESEARCH_ONLY, 10 REJECTED, 4 SUPERSEDED, and 2 CONTRADICTED; every substrate piece is partial or absent as a complete north-star contract.
- Current red class: none; the initial G-B evidence-anchor findings were corrected append-only and the single permitted renewal approved.
- Next cheapest discriminator: close B, then define the campaign evidence/approval contract in D before choosing laws in E.
- Active external blocker: none.
- Stop or escalation: any G-B coverage mismatch, unresolved sampled owner, unsupported `SATISFIED`, or unsearched `ABSENT` rejects the candidate; one renewal maximum.

DECISION THIS STAGE CAN MOVE: which of the 615 frozen donor items and eight seed hypotheses current BreadBoard satisfies, partially satisfies, contradicts, lacks, supersedes, reserves for research, or deliberately rejects.
EVIDENCE THAT WOULD MOVE IT: symbol-verified owners at the pinned ENGINE/TUI heads, actual consumers, contract-tier and freeze dispositions, focused test anchors, and a bounded consumer-universe search.
EVIDENCE PRODUCED SO FAR: 623/623 dispositions, current surface/tier inventories, exact status counts, closure-group coverage, substrate/depth audits, and append-only corrections for diagnosed raw findings.
PROVENANCE-ONLY ARTIFACTS PRODUCED SO FAR: one raw store containing provenance, four research slices, freeze output, and append-only correction records.

## Gate card and bounded charter

- Claim: every frozen donor ID and all eight seed hypotheses receive exactly one top-level disposition supported by current baseline evidence; every `SATISFIED` row names an owner and evidence, every `PARTIAL` row names missing behavior, and every `ABSENT` row is downstream of the complete B2 consumer-universe search.
- Denominator: 615 donor items + 8 seeds = 623 dispositions. Each of the 50 closure groups maps to at least one row.
- Primary risks: false satisfaction from prose or stale snapshots; false absence from an incomplete search; fabricated owner names; treating E4 evidence as product truth; rewarding shallow abstractions or duplicate authorities.
- Discriminating power: Gate G-B independently recomputes 623-of-623 coverage, samples every status, verifies symbols at both pinned heads, confirms every closure group mapping, and rejects any owner or test anchor that cannot be resolved.
- Oracle: current source, registries, generated contracts, consumers, and focused tests at the pinned heads. The assessment and historical handoffs remain claim indexes.
- Cost: at most four sessions, four bounded raw research slices, one independent review, and one renewal only if candidate bytes materially change.
- Retry: only after a changed source anchor, diagnosed search blind spot, corrected row-generation rule, or reviewer finding.
- Stop: complete coverage with Gate G-B approval, or block affected rows as `UNVERIFIED` with an exact missing prerequisite. Never infer approval or implementation priority.
- Fallback: classify uncertain mappings `RESEARCH_ONLY` or `ABSENT` only as permitted by the status rules; preserve the raw anchors and leave promotion to E/F.
- Nonclaims: B does not choose normative laws, authorize a new module or seam, change a public surface, implement a donor, or award compatibility/parity.

## Row contract

Each donor row records: ID; frozen assessment anchor; concise idea; current owner as symbol and path at head or `none`; consumers; contracts; focused test evidence; exactly one status; rationale; law relation; module-test summary where a module is proposed; promotion basis; observable acceptance condition; reuse constraint.

Allowed statuses:

- `SATISFIED`: current owner, consumer, contract, and evidence are named.
- `PARTIAL`: current owner and evidence are named, plus the exact missing behavior.
- `CONTRADICTED`: current behavior or authority conflicts with the donor claim; both sides are anchored.
- `ABSENT`: the defined consumer universe was searched and no current owner/behavior was found.
- `SUPERSEDED`: current BreadBoard behavior is stronger or simpler; the replacement owner and evidence are named.
- `RESEARCH_ONLY`: no product disposition is justified without a future research result.
- `REJECTED`: repository governance or a documented current decision deliberately excludes the donor idea.

All rows inherit `reuse_constraint: idea_only` unless an exact DSH item-level anchor is added through PROC-AMEND. A proposed module passes only if it hides meaningful policy behind a smaller interface, has at least two real adapters at its seam, improves a named change scenario, and does not duplicate an existing authority.

## Depth and duplicate-authority audit

Sixteen rows explicitly propose a module or seam and carry all seven section 6.1 answers. Eight have at least two real current adapters. Eight fail the adapter threshold and remain blocked hypotheses: DSH-DONOR-25-001, DSH-DONOR-29-025, DSH-DONOR-31-008, DSH-DONOR-36-012, DSH-DONOR-37-001, DSH-DONOR-37-003, DSH-DONOR-38-008, DSH-DONOR-38-009. Passing the adapter threshold proves only that a seam is real; it does not prove the donor behavior or authorize implementation.

The seven nouns and four protocols receive explicit primitive verdicts through `primitive-verdict-corrections.jsonl`: Definition/Event/Projection/Capability/Operation and all four protocols are vocabulary only; Entity and Resource are shallow behavior-owning generalizations and are rejected as modules. Existing specific owners remain authoritative.

| Apparent duplicate | Consumers | Survivor/authority | Lock and simplification result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python and TypeScript generated public bindings | SDKs, TUI, CLI parity | `contracts/public/operations.v2.json` + generator | intentional adapters, not duplicate authority; parity lock retained |
| Public session operations and legacy cli_bridge session routes | public SDK/TUI versus legacy clients | `/v1` public operation catalog; legacy registry disposition until zero consumers | later deletion requires consumer migration and route parity lock; no deletion earned here |
| TUI `canonicalClient` and `controlClient` | session event stream versus create/model/provider control calls | `connectCanonicalBreadboardEnginePort` composes disjoint interfaces | not duplicate authority; keep split because lifecycle/evidence semantics differ |
| Kernel event v1/v2 | registry-named compatibility consumers | contract-tier/schema-lifecycle registries | frozen/supersede policy governs migration; no untracked deletion |
| Canonical runtime and E4/audit event views | product runtime versus conformance evidence | product event owners; E4 never product truth | distinct authorities by charter; no merge into E4 |

No confirmed duplicate authority earns a deletion packet in B. S5 remains PARTIAL until every frozen/superseded consumer is named and migrated.
